question: How do maturity alignment and finite-sample selection objectives change hypothetical hedging risk under costs and model shift?
prior_data_use: V1 USD/JPY 2021–2025 results have already been examined. V2 retrospective yearly evaluations are exploratory, not restored untouched tests. The protocol is source-frozen, not externally preregistered.

historical.inner_validation: Two calendar years immediately before outer year; initial fit uses earlier labels with target END before validation starts; final refit includes past validation labels whose end precedes outer year
historical.hyperparameter_metric: Validation mean QLIKE against 21-observation average squared return; term uses h=21; flat uses h=1 extrapolation; all scoring target windows wholly within validation
historical.features: V1 seven causal features; training-only scaling and mean-ratio log correction; ridge_term fits each remaining horizon directly
historical.premium: Identical start rolling63 BS premium per episode across all models and policies
historical.band_rule: Trade to nearest boundary of a constant delta-centered no-trade band, not to its center; common midpoint entry and terminal liquidation
historical.primary_comparison: ridge_term versus ridge_flat, band05, 5bps, paired squared net loss, separately by currency
historical.statistics: Per-currency moving-block bootstrap over chronological episodes, block3 primary, block1/6 sensitivity; Holm adjustment for six currency tests, centered block-bootstrap approximate two-sided p-values; no pooled independent-currency claims
historical.holdout_rule: The 2026 period was present in the archived raw source but not scored in V1; evaluate only after source protocol freeze, once, without changing model grid from its results. Short period and dependence limit confirmation.

simulation.primary: Heston matched,64 validation paths,5bps: joint_mse minus forecast_first test MSE, independent full-procedure replicates as inference units
simulation.reference_oracle: Per replicate chosen-model class reference optimum evaluated on a separate large Monte Carlo sample; noisy, retrospective finite-class information benchmark, never a deployable selector
output_requirements: net MSE variance and bias squared decomposition

convex_extension.purpose: Explainable direct-risk-learning comparator, not claimed novel algorithm
convex_extension.class: BS delta plus fixed causal features linear in coefficients; transaction costs represented by absolute-trade epigraphs; sample CVaR90 linear program
convex_extension.position_constraints: Enforced on training states only; out-of-sample violations explicitly reported, no claim of global bound
convex_extension.constraints: No clipping in optimized class; report actual out-of-sample positions, fees, risk, training LP residual and independently recomputed objective

claims: Finite empirical study with strong baselines, actual numerical runs and post-selection limits. P-measure second moments supplied to BS delta are control heuristics, not market implied Q-volatility. No market profits, original algorithm, acceptance guarantee or absolute technical perfection claim.
